chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Bābawayh, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Walīd, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yāsīn al-Ḍarīr, from Ḥarīz, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who has milk with him: may he perform wudu (ablution) from it for salat (prayer)? He said: No. It is only water and earth.

Al-Shaykh Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This report indicates that whatever is not designated by the name of water is not permissible to use, and it conforms to the outward meaning of the Book and what is established in the principles.

key_terms.الصَّعِيدُ: earth, used for tayammum as an alternative purification medium
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act of worship requiring ritual purity
key_terms.اللَّبَنُ: milk, mentioned here as a liquid that cannot be used for wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْكِتَابِ: the Qur'an, whose outward meaning supports this ruling
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water, the valid substance for wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأُ: to perform wudu (ablution) for ritual purity

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed with milk if no water is available?
ai.summary: This hadith states that wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) is not valid with milk, and that purification is restricted to water or, when applicable, earth for tayammum. Al-Ṭūsī explains that substances not legally called water cannot be used for ritual purification, in agreement with the apparent meaning of the Qur'an and established legal principles.
